# SidebarLayout

The shell of an app with a `Sidebar`: the sidebar beside the page from 640px up, in view while the page scrolls, and a sticky top bar with the sidebar's menu button below 640px. It renders the page's `<main>` and starts with a "Skip to content" link.

```tsx
import { SidebarLayout } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/sidebar/sidebar-layout";
```

## Example

```tsx
<SidebarLayout
  sidebar={<Sidebar label="Main" sections={sections} currentPath={pathname} />}
  header={<TextField label="Search" hideLabel type="search" />}
>
  <Outlet />
</SidebarLayout>
```

## Usage

The phone menu opens once JavaScript has loaded (after hydration); the links are in the server HTML from 640px up.

Use `AuthLayout` for the sign-in pages.

## Use instead when

- Use `StackedLayout` instead when the navigation is a `Navbar` across the top.

## Props

Type: `SidebarLayoutProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `"div" \| "main"` | `"main"` | The element around the page. Pass `"div"` when the layout renders inside a page that already has a `<main>`, since a document has one. |
| `bleed` | `boolean` |  | Removes the padding around the page, for content that runs edge to edge (a map, a cover photo). |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The page. It renders inside the page's `<main>`. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: height and margins (`min-h-96`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `header` | `ReactNode` |  | A bar above the page: a search field, the page's actions. From 640px up it runs across the top of the page, beside the sidebar; below, it shares the top bar with the menu button. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `sidebar` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The app's `Sidebar`. It sits beside the page from 640px up, and is a menu button in the top bar below. |
| `skipLabel` | `string` | `"Skip to content"` | The text of the link that skips the sidebar, shown when it has keyboard focus. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `navbar`: Not a prop. The bar above the page is `header`: `<SidebarLayout sidebar={…} header={…}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
